gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker SOLIX S5000 has two unequal solar inputs (11–60 V / 17 A / 1,000 W and 16–165 V / 17 A / 2,000 W), so the two 400 W panels in its $3,599.99 kit (48 V, 8.33 A each) wired in series at 96 V fit only the 16–165 V input, and that only the BP5000 battery fits it and it does not work with Anker's Home Power Panel.
standout_why: Compared against StormWatts (cited), PowerSized, Prepared States, Lights On Labs and our own under-$3,000 page; solargenadvisor.com failed with a certificate error and was not read. PowerSized already has the Apex 300 + 2 × 500 W wiring (one panel per input, 98.2 V in series, 26.6 A in parallel, two MC4-to-XT60 cables in the box). StormWatts has input limits and series/parallel notes for kits up to $3,299. Our under-$3,000 page has the Elite 400 + 2 × 350 W parallel-only limit. None of them lists the S5000 + 2 × 400 W kit or the Apex 200 + B500K + 2 × 500 W kit, the two largest kits under $4,000. None gives the S5000's per-input volts and amps, its battery and Home Power Panel exclusions, or the Apex 200's 60–280 V input that takes the two 500 W panels as one series string.
decides: Compatibility confirms the S5000 + 2 × 400 W kit as the largest-battery choice under $4,000: the panels fit and use 800 W of a 3,000 W solar limit. But Anker's product page, read today, says orders placed on or after November 6 ship within 11–12 weeks and that the 400 W panel ships separately, which conflicts with 'ships now' in our kit table. This was a single read through the fetch tool, so re-check it in a browser before publishing. If it holds, the S5000 kit becomes the larger option for a shopper who can wait, and the ships-now pick has to come from the ALLPOWERS R3500 kits or the BLUETTI 5kWh RV kit. For the 7,680 Wh Apex 200 + B500K + 2 × 500 W pre-order ($3,986.20 link price), the two panels run as one series string into the high-voltage input; on the Apex 300 each panel needs its own input.

findings.label: Solar input 1 (low-PV)
findings.note: Spec table row 'Solar Panel Input 1'. The page names a 'Low-PV / Car Input Port' and a 'High-PV Input Port' but does not name the connector types.

findings.label: Solar input 2 (high-PV)
findings.value: 16–165 V, 17 A max, 2,000 W max; 3,000 W solar combined
findings.note: Spec table row 'Solar Panel Input 2'; the charging section lists 'Solar: 3,000W Max'. Anker's specs blog (https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/anker-solix-s5000-specs, read the same day) repeats 1,000 W + 2,000 W = 3,000 W.

findings.product: Anker SOLIX PS400 Bifacial (the kit's 400 W panel)
findings.label: Panel output and cables in the box
findings.value: PV output 48 V, 8.33 A; box has two 8.2 ft (2.5 m) solar charging cables and one 1.6 ft (0.5 m) XT-60i solar charging cable
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX PS400 Bifacial Portable Solar Panel - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: These are operating figures; the page lists no open-circuit voltage. The page also says orders placed on or after October 30 are expected to begin shipping in early December.

findings.label: How the kit's two panels fit the inputs (arithmetic)
findings.value: Series: 2 × 48 V = 96 V, over the 60 V limit of input 1 and inside the 16–165 V of input 2. Parallel: 2 × 8.33 A = 16.66 A, under the 17 A limit. 800 W of panels against a 3,000 W solar limit leaves 2,200 W of headroom.
findings.note: Arithmetic from the PS400's operating figures and the S5000 input table. Open-circuit voltage is higher than 48 V and is unsourced, so a parallel pair on the 60 V input and a three-panel series string are not confirmed.

findings.label: Kit price, free gift and shipping notice on Anker's page
findings.value: $3,599.99 with a free 400 W solar panel; 'Orders placed on or after November 6th will ship within 11 - 12 weeks'; 'If your order includes the 400W solar panel, it will ship separately.'
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S5000 + 400W Bifacial Solar Panel - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Conflicts with 'ships now' in our kit table (read 2026-11-17); verify in a browser. The same page lists S5000 alone at $2,599.99 and S5000 + 1 × 400 W at $3,099.99. The collection page showed $4,399.99 for the one-panel kit, so the collection price and the product-page price differ.

findings.label: Battery and home-panel exclusions
findings.value: BP5000 expansion battery is 'exclusive to S5000'; 'Third-party batteries and previous models, including BP3800 and BP3000, are incompatible'; 'Anker SOLIX S5000 is not compatible with Anker SOLIX Home Power Panel'
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S5000 + 400W Bifacial Solar Panel - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: From the page FAQ. BP5000 is $2,000.00 as an add-on. Anker's specs blog says it expands to 30 kWh with 'up to five compatible expansion batteries'. The same page sells a Home Backup Kit at $499.99.

findings.label: Apex 200 solar inputs
findings.value: High-voltage MC4 input: 60–280 V, up to 2,000 W, 'supports compatible panels connected in series'. Low-voltage XT60 input: up to 1,000 W. Combined 3,000 W.
findings.note: Body text; the Tech Specs table was empty in the fetch. StormWatts gives the XT60 input as 12–60 V, 25 A (https://stormwatts.com/articles/solar-generator-kits-compared-same-panel-watts/, read 2026-11-18).

findings.label: How the kit's two 500 W panels fit (arithmetic)
findings.value: Two SORA 500 in series = 98.2 V, inside the 60–280 V high-voltage MC4 input, so the pair runs as one string. One panel alone (98.2 / 2 = 49.1 V) is under that input's 60 V floor and has to use the XT60 input. In parallel the pair is 26.6 A, over the 25 A StormWatts gives for the XT60 input.
findings.source_title: Best Solar Generators of 2026: Kits by Battery Size (PowerSized)
findings.note: The 98.2 V and 26.6 A figures are PowerSized's, stated for two SORA 500 panels. BLUETTI's own 500 W panel page showed no Voc or Isc in the fetch. Contrast: on the Apex 300 (two inputs, each 1,200 W, 12–60 V, 20 A per PowerSized) the same two panels cannot share an input and go one per input.

findings.label: In the box, expansion and shipping
findings.value: Listed box contents: Apex 200, AC charging cable (1.5 m / 4.92 ft), grounding screw, quick start guide; no solar cable listed. 'Each Apex 200 supports up to six compatible expansion batteries' (B300K or B500K). 'The Apex 200 is expected to ship in late January for orders placed on or after Nov. 14.'
findings.note: The in-box list shown is the station's; the kit page did not list the panels' or battery's box contents in the fetch. Store price $4,196.00 confirmed by storecheck the same day; the link price of $3,986.20 is from our table.

findings.label: Connector and shipping
findings.value: MC4 connector ('With a universal MC4 connector, SORA 500 works with almost any power station'); $849.00; 'expected to ship in late January for orders placed on or after Nov. 18'
findings.note: The same page also shows a listing line 'ships from 11.28', which conflicts with the late-January notice. BLUETTI's MC4 extension cable (5 m / 10 m, 30 A, $59.00) is listed as compatible with the SORA 500, one cable set per panel in a parallel setup.

findings.source_title: Best Solar Generators of 2026: Kits by Battery Size (PowerSized)
findings.note: PowerSized's statement of BLUETTI's US page; not new to the results ChatGPT got. Kit price $3,299.00 confirmed by storecheck on bluettipower.com the same day.
